acceptance_criteria: Active or plausibly active emergencies (gas, CO, fire, smoke, sparking, overheating, live/exposed wiring, flooding near electricity, structural collapse) are intercepted before retrieval, planning or workflow.
notes: Measured on an engineer-written tuning corpus only (52 active rows): 52/52 intercepted, and safety is decided before every other stage. Not certification evidence; no sealed pool; not reviewed by a Home Safety/Policy Reviewer.

acceptance_criteria: Active reports are distinguished from education, history, hypotheticals and resolved incidents; recall and false-positive rate are measured separately.
notes: Per-clause framing check (emergencyFraming.ts) keeps any present-tense cue active. Tuning corpus: 0 false positives in 45 benign rows. A framing in one clause never silences an emergency in another. Tuning evidence only; unseen phrasing may still be missed or over-fired.

acceptance_criteria: An emergency interaction offers only safety information; it creates no ordinary next actions and continues no workflow.
notes: The emergency answer is BLOCKED/IMMEDIATE_SAFETY with no suggestions of its own, and the finalizer never adds next actions to a blocked result (code-traced and source-asserted, not run end to end).

acceptance_criteria: Emergency recall and false-positive rate are measured separately on a held-out corpus.
notes: NOT MET: only the tuning corpus exists (recall 52/52, false positives 0/45). The gate needs a sealed, independently authored corpus and a Home Safety/Policy Reviewer; those are people-blocked.

acceptance_criteria: Authored guidance comes from a versioned catalogue with owner, evidence basis, scope, exclusions, review and dates, with lint and a coverage report.
notes: Governance metadata and lint done. All 7 entries have evidence basis UNRECORDED and safety and editorial review PENDING; no topic inventory or held-out demand measure exists yet.

acceptance_criteria: Each substantive answer facet declares one answer mode.
notes: Mode assigned by operation, conservatively (no CALCULATION until inputs declare provenance), shown as a label on the answer card. A composed answer now carries one mode per facet (facetModes, in delivery order) and each facet's first block is labelled with its own mode; the response-level mode is then null so facets are never collapsed. USER_DOCUMENT is not built. Unit and render tested; the composed labels were not exercised against a real composed turn in a database or viewed in a browser.

acceptance_criteria: Regenerate creates a new attempt linked to the original, preserves both, and never repeats a write.
notes: Backend service, route, link, idempotency and refusal rules unit-tested against stubs; frontend control and hook tested. Not exercised against a real database or browser.

acceptance_criteria: Follow-up resolution uses a bounded structured conversation summary.
notes: The summary gates follow-up continuation, supplies the canonical entity for task follow-ups, and is now the source of carried slots for elliptical follow-ups (this home, settled turns, 2-hour window). Unit-tested with stubbed Prisma; not run against a real database. Slot carry no longer counts turns older than the summary's recency window.

acceptance_criteria: Every carried entity and result reference keeps its canonical identifier and authorization scope.
notes: Entity references carry canonical id and property scope in the summary. 'Complete it' and reschedule/update/cancel/archive/reopen/mark of a single listed maintenance task now resolve by canonical id (launch entity or supplied task id) instead of a title; several tasks name nothing. A single listed inventory item can be updated by id ('update it' opens the correction review for that item). Other entity types still use the title rewrite; a deleted entity is never acted on or matched by title. Unit-tested with stubbed Prisma; not run against a real database.

acceptance_criteria: Property switch, access loss, entity deletion or result expiry invalidate incompatible context and disclose the reset.
notes: Reconciliation and disclosure are enforced for ordinary follow-ups with live checks: a home switch, a home the person can no longer reach, a deleted entity (maintenance task, inventory item) and an expired result each remove the affected context and the person is told. Entity types other than maintenance task and inventory item are assumed to exist. The slot-carry path does not use these checks (it reads this home's settled turns only). Unit-tested with stubbed Prisma; the real checks are tested for scoping only, not against a real database.

acceptance_criteria: No unlimited raw history to a model; retention, truncation and sensitive-field policy are explicit and tested.
notes: Turn, age, field and byte limits and a forbidden-key policy are tested; no model receives history anywhere (provider register allowlists). Retention of stored executions is governed elsewhere.

acceptance_criteria: Cross-session workflow continuity uses canonical workflow identity.
notes: Cross-session continuity resumes canonical workflow identity only (typed workKey prefixes: journey, decision thread, work item, project, claim, DIY, renovation, monitor, execution and more), scoped to the user and the home, re-checking existence, supersession, completion and role, and reporting a plain outcome (AVAILABLE, DELETED, COMPLETED, STALE, ACCESS_LOST, SUPERSEDED) with no row when it cannot resume. This already existed in the Work destination (resolveAskWork); D27 clauses are now pinned by crossSessionResumeConformance.test.js. Conversation text and slots do not cross sessions (the summary is session-scoped). Stub-tested only; the access-lost service path is source-asserted because running it needs the account-eligibility database lookup.

acceptance_criteria: A reusable parameterised suite of at least 300 distinct home-record read cases across the EVAL-019 partitions with zero wrong results.
notes: 415 cases pass (VALUE, MISSING_DATA, ENTITY, AUTHORIZATION, DATE, UNIT, BOUNDARY, FORMULA_BRANCH as read-mode branch); mutation checks fail the suite when property scoping or the audience floor is removed. Covers the reader and formatter against an in-memory database, not a real database, and not the routing from a message to a data point (BICC-GATE-001/003 held-out). Two defects found and fixed (an invalid date threw; a single-word enum kept its capitals).

acceptance_criteria: A reusable parameterised suite of at least 300 distinct calculation cases across the EVAL-019 partitions with zero wrong input, date, unit, branch, boundary, missing-data or numeric results.
notes: 753 distinct cases pass over all eight partitions; expected values come from exact integer arithmetic or hand-written rules, separate from the code. Covers the capital-plan calculators (growth, cost basis at a date, point estimate, funding plan, deposit rate, date and amount readers) the mortgage-rate resolver (units, bounds, precedence), and the pure break-even and mortgage arithmetic (level payments checked against published figures, full-term payoff, debt projection invariants, break-even year and label helpers). and the reserve fund recalculation (run against an in-memory store with the clock frozen: point estimate by posture, proportional balance share, near-term shortfall vs smoothed monthly amount capped at the horizon, confirmed allocations kept, retirement of resolved and vanished items). The break-even service's database-backed compute is NOT covered. Two month-counting rules coexist (Ask's funding plan counts calendar months, the reserve fund counts whole months); not reconciled. AUTHORIZATION covers the two capital handlers denying access before any read. First run found a real rounding defect (fixed). Fixed matrix: partition coverage, no population claim. Gate applies when calculation mode is delivered (BICC-1C.1).
